calls.reason: OpenAI's own filings report an $852B private valuation, about $2B a month in revenue and 1B weekly users. But the forecast has no deadline or measure, and nothing in the packet shows OpenAI has reached Google or Meta scale.

The Kantrowitz piece Zitron cites calls it a smooth ride so far and treats the danger as future competition. Reports from November 2023 show strong adoption, and nothing shows customer losses or a business crisis before the firing.

In the FT interview, Altman said training costs kept OpenAI unprofitable and that he expected to raise a lot more. Semafor reported staged Microsoft funding, much of it as compute, while expenses rose. Both point to real dependence on outside capital.
The condition never happened: OpenAI said it did not lose a single employee when the crisis ended. That leaves the conditional prediction untested rather than right or wrong.

Bloomberg reported that by the post date the board had resisted investor pressure to bring Altman back and chose Shear instead. The WilmerHale review found finances did not drive the firing. Both cut against a board proven entirely beholden.

TechSpot and PC Gamer reported a 2023 SemiAnalysis estimate of about $694,444 to $1M a day to run ChatGPT. That matches 'hundreds of thousands' a day, and reported losses of about $540M fit the cost concern.
